tagline: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib — Sacred Golden-Domed Sikh Shrine in Heart of New Delhi

overview.short: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib is one of the most prominent Sikh gurdwaras in Delhi, known for its association with the eighth Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan, and its holy sarovar.
overview.description: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib was originally a bungalow (haveli) belonging to Raja Jai Singh of Amber (Jaipur) in the 17th century, known as Jaisinghpura Palace. The eighth Sikh Guru, Guru Har Krishan Ji, resided here during his stay in Delhi in 1664 when smallpox and cholera epidemics broke out. The Guru gave clean water from the well in the haveli to the sick, which cured numerous sufferers. Today, the pristine sarovar (holy pool), gleaming golden dome, giant 24/7 Langar hall feeding tens of thousands daily, and tranquil marble parikrama make it a world-renowned spiritual haven of selfless service and peace.

faq.q: What are the opening timings of Gurudwara Bangla Sahib?
faq.a: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The holy sanctum, sarovar, and Langar hall welcome people of all faiths, backgrounds, and nationalities without any discrimination.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee or dress code at Gurudwara Bangla Sahib?
faq.a: Entry is 100% free. All visitors are required to cover their heads (scarves are provided free at the entrance), remove footwear, and wash their feet at the water channels before stepping onto the marble parikrama.

faq.q: How do I reach Gurudwara Bangla Sahib by Delhi Metro?
faq.a: The nearest metro stations are Shivaji Stadium on the Airport Express Line (approx. 500 metres walk) and Patel Chowk on the Yellow Line (approx. 700 metres walk). Rajiv Chowk interchange station is also within 1 km.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Gurudwara Bangla Sahib?
faq.a: The winter and spring months between October and March offer the most pleasant weather in Delhi. Visiting during early dawn (Amrit Vela) or twilight allows you to witness the golden dome illuminated against the evening sky.
